guidance: Globally unique identifier for the resource. Use a persistent, resolvable IRI when possible.
Use owl:Class for classes. For individuals, the ontology class it is an instance of. More than one @type may be used for individuals.
Information about access to the resource. One of: CONFIDENTIAL, NON_PUBLIC, PUBLIC, RESTRICTED, SENSITIVE, from EU structured vocabulary on rights.
Use when the software or dataset is relevant to a particular chemical, substance, material, or chemical class.
Agent responsible for creating or producing the resource.
At least include agent(s) responsible for curating the metadata entry of the resource in the knowledge base. Also agents curating the data itself can be added.
Human-readable description of the resource.
URL providing access to a distribution. Tripper converts the nested property into an annotation on a generated dcat:Distribution blank node.
Direct link to a downloadable file. Recommended when the resource has a directly downloadable representation.
Format of the distribution. Use distribution.mediaType if format exists in IANA.
Format of the distribution, for example text/csv or application/json. Mediatype options can be found at IANA.
Date on which this particular distribution was formally issued.
Search keyword or tag.
Short human-readable label.
Licence under which the resource is made available or may be reused.
Upstream dataset or entity from which the dataset was processed or derived.
Agent responsible for making the resource available. This may differ from its creator.
Date of formal issuance or publication. Use an ISO 8601 value compatible with xsd:dateTime.
Person or organisation owning or managing rights over the resource.
Main controlled category or SSbD thematic area of the resource.
Human-readable title of the resource. For classes, label is preferred.
Version name or identifier.
The process that generated the resource (typically a dataset). Particularly important to define assessments, either as types or individuals.
